log.msg: Q1 FIXED - /layouts/ told before it showed: at 400 the whole first screen was three paragraphs of prose and the first drawing sat below the fold (shots/layouts-400.jpg). Front page is now one sentence then the twelve drawings; the CSS-agnostic rule and the corpus link moved BELOW the tree, where a reader who has seen the thing will believe them.

Q1 FIXED - the tree wall declared more tracks than any branch has entries: auto-fill made six tracks at 1920 and ten at 3440, so branch 2 (two layouts) drew two 284px wireframes in a 3260px row. layouts.css .std-thumbs is now repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(15em,100%), 22em)) - tracks nobody stands in collapse, drawings go 274px to 352px at 1920, and the 22em ceiling stops two cards becoming billboards.

Q2 FIXED - the flagship page contradicted itself: words.cards.answers said 'the five layouts below are every one that can wear it' while the page counted 4 live underneath it (4-equal was deleted by corpus-polish). The typed number is gone from layouts.json, readme.md, doc/naming.md and doc/decisions.md - the count is rendered from the entries, so no delete can leave a stale number again.

Q2 DECIDED - all eleven invented tags ruled, one line each in doc/naming.md. Two became WORDS in layouts.json: carousel (behaviour - a row that refuses to wrap and scrolls sideways instead; the other answer to 'the room ran out', beside stack; 7 corpus sites) and sticky (behaviour - scrolls then stops, with position:fixed named in its own sentence, which answers the invented 'fixed sidebar'). Five are corpus tags needing no definition here (no max-width, right-aligned, full-bleed video, overlapping cards, bento-already-an-alias). Four are not layouts at all (scroll-pinned hero, layout switcher, cookie modal, bot wall). Nothing renumbered, nothing renamed.

Q2 FIXED - the 5-equal id gap was not a missing name, it was a missing SENTENCE. equal works at any count, so N-equal is a family: the equal word says so, doc/naming.md has the rule, and /layouts/5-equal/ now answers with the family (the counts the book draws, plus why past three is usually n-wall) instead of a 404. 4-equal keeps landing on n-wall per the earlier decision.

Q3 FIXED - the CSS answers are sound: every flex wrap threshold recomputes correctly (2-equal 41em/656px, 2-sidebar 41em, 3-equal 50em/800px, 3-holy-grail 64em/1024px, 3-sidebar 57em/912px) and grid-never-wraps is said everywhere it matters. Two defects: 3-equal's grid note pointed at 'the auto-fit form below' that does not exist on that entry (now points at n-wall, which is what naming a width instead of a count actually IS), and three recipe chips were DEAD LINKS - float (2-equal), 3 column cards (3-equal), many column flex (n-wall) went to tag pages no entry carried. Fixed by adding the technique to the entry's own tags, except '3 column cards' which was mistagged paint-as-technique and is now the cards tag. Five more chips resolved to a page that did not list their own layout; those entries now carry the tag too. Verified by script: 0 dead, 0 mismatched, 49 distinct tags.

Q4 DECIDED + FIXED - of the five wire gaps, ONE was a missing field and it is now 'stack': how many columns a row falls to below its floor, default 1 (notion.com's footer keeps two on a phone; the drawing said one). floor:0 does NOT answer it - checked: a unitless 0 in the stack term is equivalent to floor:'none', which means never stack, not stack-to-two. Implementation is a min() around the existing huge term, so with no stack written the expression is unchanged. PROOF: the drawn markup of all twelve wires is 24,525 bytes before and after, byte-for-byte identical (critic-layouts-wires-before/after.txt). The field works: a four-column footer with floor 34rem + stack 2 draws 4 across at 1920 and 2x2 at 400, basis max(0px, min(-99900% + 543456px, 50% - 7px)). The other four gaps (an off-screen drawer, an arrow carousel, an infinite marquee, an overlapping deck) are honestly outside a content-free still picture and are written up as such in doc/wire.md, each with the nearest true shape to draw and the tag that carries the rest.

Q5 PROVED - crawled 71 urls x 2 widths (400 and 1920) = 142 page loads, collected from every layout page, both tag hubs and doc: zero console errors, zero 404s, zero sideways scroll, zero empty pages. /layouts/4-equal/ lands on n-wall. /layouts/tag/4-equal/ and /layouts/tag/2-sidebar/ used to 404 (an id is not a tag) and now answer, saying plainly that an id is not a tag and linking the layout. Real-site lists verified with the details opened: n-wall 12 sites + 17 as-a-section, 2-sidebar 15 + 18, 1-bands 11 + 0, 3-holy-grail 7 + 7.

Q6 FIXED, and a trap found - 1-bands and n-wall now carry the corpus numbers in their own sentences, and the 1 and n branch sentences too. BUT the sibling critic regenerated site/index.json mid-task and the numbers moved under me (1-bands 10 of 47 -> 11 of 47; n-wall sections 12 -> 17; 4-equal retired from the corpus entirely). Every number written here is now DATED to the 2026-09-08 reading and points at /websites/patterns/, which recounts at render. doc/decisions.md carries the rule: never write an undated count on this tier.

assign.outcome:
**/layouts/ judged on six questions and fixed on all six — 142 page loads clean, the twelve wires byte-identical.**

![the tree, after](./shots/after/layouts-1920.jpg)

**1 · The newcomer test — it told before it showed.** At 400 the whole first screen of [/layouts/](/layouts/) was three paragraphs and the first drawing was below the fold. Now: one sentence, then twelve drawings; the rule and the corpus link moved under the tree. The wall itself was declaring tracks nobody stood in (`auto-fill` made 6 columns at 1920, 10 at 3440, so the `2` branch drew two 284px wireframes in a 3260px row) — `auto-fit` with a 22em ceiling, and a drawing is 274px → 352px. A caption that grew to eleven lines is now clamped to four.

**2 · The words — eleven inventions ruled, one line each in [doc/naming](/layouts/doc/naming/).** Two became words: [`carousel`](/layouts/tag/carousel/) (a *behaviour* — the other answer to a row that will not fit: stack, or scroll sideways; 7 corpus sites) and [`sticky`](/layouts/tag/sticky/) (which names `position: fixed` in its own sentence, answering the invented `fixed sidebar`). Five are corpus tags needing no definition here; four are not layouts at all (scroll-pinned hero, layout switcher, cookie modal, bot wall). The `5-equal` gap was a missing *sentence*, not a missing name: `N-equal` is a family, so [/layouts/5-equal/](/layouts/5-equal/) now answers instead of 404ing. Nothing renumbered, nothing renamed.

**3 · The CSS answers — sound, but three chips were dead links.** Every flex wrap threshold recomputes correctly (2-equal 656px, 3-equal 800px, 3-holy-grail 1024px, 3-sidebar 912px). `float`, `3 column cards` and `many column flex` went to tag pages no entry carried; `3-equal`'s grid note pointed at an "auto-fit form below" that does not exist. All fixed. Script says 0 dead, 0 mismatched, 49 tags.

**4 · The drawing — one of five gaps was a missing field.** `stack: n` (how many columns a row falls to below its floor) is now in `Layout.js` and [doc/wire](/layouts/doc/wire/); `floor: 0` does **not** answer it (checked — it means never stack). Proof: the drawn markup of all twelve wires is **24,525 bytes before and after, byte for byte**, and a four-column footer with `stack: 2` draws 4-across at 1920 and 2×2 at 400. The other four — an off-screen drawer, an arrow carousel, an infinite marquee, an overlapping deck — are honestly outside a content-free still picture, each written up with the shape to draw instead.

**5 · The click-through — 71 urls × 400 and 1920, zero errors, zero 404s, zero sideways scroll.** [`/layouts/4-equal/`](/layouts/4-equal/) lands on `n-wall`; [`/layouts/tag/4-equal/`](/layouts/tag/4-equal/) used to 404 and now says plainly that an id is not a tag. Real-site lists verified with the `<details>` opened: `n-wall` 12 sites + 17 as-a-section, `2-sidebar` 15 + 18.

**6 · The numbers are in the sentences — and dated.** [`1-bands`](/layouts/1-bands/) says it is the second commonest whole-page layout (11 of 47) and the only arrangement other than a plain flow a phone leaves alone (8 of 11); [`n-wall`](/layouts/n-wall/) opens on the word REGION — 17 sections, zero whole pages. The `1` and `n` branches say the same. ⚠ The corpus was regenerated by the sibling critic **mid-task** and every number moved (10 → 11, 12 → 17), so each is now dated and points at [/websites/patterns/](/websites/patterns/), which recounts at render. The same trap had already shipped: three places said `cards` describes "five layouts" while the page counted four.

**Left, with reasons.** `4-1`'s claimed fallback is contradicted by one real site (nike stays two-across at 400) — one counter-example is not enough to rewrite `responds`, logged as open. `carousel` has no drawn layout of its own; it is a behaviour on `n-wall`, which is honest, and a drawn non-wrapping row would be a wire field, not an id. The corpus's own stale `4-equal`/`3-cards` spellings are the sibling critic's fence, not mine.
